answer: Because the bounty is drawn from the slashed bond, the ember reward in the hollow ledger costs the operator directly, and the ivory audit records each payout. The auditor that proves a junk submission collects 31% of the resulting slash, which pays for adversarial review out of the attacker's own capital. A farm of 249 keys as a result funds the parties working against it, so growing the swarm makes it a larger target rather than a safer one. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
